summary: A 93-foot steel fire tower from 1932 near Tarboro; a 2018 state survey found it no longer in use but still standing and eligible for the National Register.

facts.design: Four-sided truss frame of galvanized steel with an enclosed one-room cabin under a pyramidal roof
facts.agency: North Carolina Division of Forest Resources

events.note: Erected about four miles southwest of Tarboro as a 93-foot steel tower; the 2018 survey gives the date as ca. 1932.
A new towerman's residence was built at the tower, per the 1958-60 biennial report.
NCDOT survey found the tower no longer in use but still in its original location, and recommended it eligible for the National Register under Criterion A. The SHPO concurred on November 15, 2018.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 1930-32 biennial report stresses a glass-enclosed cab. The 2018 survey describes metal sheets below nine-light windows, some broken. The story reports both descriptions.
The biennial report gives 1932 and the survey gives ca. 1932. They agree on the year.

sources.title: Historic Structures Survey Report, Widen NC 111 from US 64 Alternate to NC 122, Edgecombe County (ER 18-3396), with SHPO review letter
sources.publisher: North Carolina Department of Natural and Cultural Resources, State Historic Preservation Office

notes_for_editor: Current condition rests on the NCDOT historic structures survey (report transmitted October 15, 2018) and the SHPO concurrence of November 15, 2018. Nothing later was found, so the story says 'by 2018' rather than 'today'; a site visit or Forest Service check would confirm present condition and access. The record's status 'unknown' is now 'standing' as of 2018. The Fountain tower (ca. 1959, demolished 2017) is a separate lookout and is not in this record. A search snippet suggested a Forest Service office address on McKendree Church Road; it was not checked and is not used. No fires were found in the sources read. No photos were added: the survey figures belong to the NCDOT report and their reuse terms are unknown.
